steps.path: Click the 5h, 7d or Cost chip in the bar along the bottom of the window
steps.headline: Clicking a usage or cost chip opens a Usage window instead of a website.
steps.changed: A new Usage window. Top: every limit and balance right now, each with a button to that provider's own site. Below: your history, same as Settings.
steps.notice: One click from any chat shows how close you are to every limit, and which provider and model used the most this week.
steps.risk: The chips no longer open claude.ai directly; that is now the claude.ai button inside the window.

steps.headline: Where should the full usage view live in Settings?
steps.notice: The outside tester could not find usage under Cloud providers, and saw the history before the limits there.
steps.risk: Either way the numbers are identical; this only decides where you look.

variants.label: Top of Cloud providers
variants.summary: What you asked for first: history at the top of the Cloud providers page, limits stay on each provider's card below.
variants.risk: Nothing named Usage in Settings, and the limits are below the history.

variants.label: Its own Usage tab
variants.summary: A Usage tab next to Cloud providers, laid out exactly like the popup: limits first, then history. Cloud providers keeps its cards and new lines.
variants.risk: One more tab in Assistant settings.

steps.path: Settings → Assistant settings → Cloud providers → ChatGPT
steps.headline: The ChatGPT card shows its per-model limit and extra credits under the plan bars.
steps.changed: Two new lines appear only when ChatGPT reports them: a limit that applies to one model, and extra credits left.
steps.notice: A stop caused by one model's limit, or credits running out, is visible here instead of unexplained.
steps.risk: ChatGPT does not document these figures, so a line may vanish if they change what they send.

steps.path: Settings → Assistant settings → Cloud providers → OpenRouter
steps.headline: The OpenRouter card shows your credit left once your key works.
steps.changed: A Credit left line on the connected OpenRouter card, refreshed every few minutes and after each reply.
steps.notice: You see credit running down before a reply fails for lack of it.
steps.risk: Only shown for a key that works; a broken or missing key shows no balance.

steps.path: The Settings gear and the usage chips
steps.headline: How should the app warn you that a limit or balance is running low?
steps.today: The 5h and 7d chips already turn amber at 50% and red at 80%. A red dot on the Settings gear already means backup is failing.
steps.problem: My earlier proposal (amber 80%, red 95%, on the gear) clashes with both: two colour scales, and a red gear dot that could mean two different things.
steps.proposal: Pick one. None of these moves the chips' existing colours.

options.label: Amber gear dot
options.summary: An amber dot on the gear when any limit passes 80% or OpenRouter credit drops under $2. Never red.
pros: Visible even with the chips turned off.
Red keeps meaning backup trouble only.
cons: One more dot that can appear on the gear.

options.label: Chips only
options.summary: Keep today's chip colours as the only warning; add nothing.
cons: No warning at all if the chips are turned off, and none for OpenRouter credit.
